messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: release of seewave 1.6.0
parts:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (1.6.0) is now on CRAN.

Here are the NEWS

NEW FEATURES
o kl.dist(): a new function to compute Kullback-Leibler distance
between two spectra.
o ks.dist(): a new function to compute Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance
between two spectra.
o notefreq(): a new function to compute musical note frequency.
o spectro(): a new argument 'oma' giving the size of the outer margins.

OTHER CHANGES
o ama(): a small bug regarding the argument 'f' has been fixed.
o covspectro(), csh(), dfreq(), dynspec(), ffilter(), lfs(),
meanspec(), spectro(), spectro3D(), wf(): are now faster.
o dfreq(): a new argument 'bandpass' to limit the search of the
dominant frequency in a specified frequency band.
o env(): is now faster when using the argument 'msmooth' (thanks to
Emilio A. Laca!).
o spectro(): a small bug regarding the size of the labels have been
fixed.
o th(): should be faster.
o timer(): is now much faster (thanks to Emilio A. Laca!).

DEPRECATED & DEFUNCT
o csh(), dfreq(), dynspec(), ffilter(), lfs(), meanspec(),
spectro(), spectro3D(), wf(): 'pb' argument has been deleted.

As usually the web page as been updated: http://rug.mnhn.fr/seewave

Please report bugs. There might be some as an important part of the code
has changed.

Best regards,

Jerome

parts:
Hello Emilio,

Thanks for the note. I am not sure about what you mean with "true p or s".

I tried this without troubles:

# seewave favourite sound sample that starts with a pause
> data(tico)

# running timer
> res1 <- timer(tico,f=22050,threshold=5,msmooth=c(100,0))
# which gives with apparently right labels
> res1
$s
[1] 0.3226313 0.2135728 0.2999108 0.1772200

$p
[1] 0.06816154 0.20902873 0.16358770 0.24083745 0.09542616

$r
[1] 1.304094

# cut tico to have a sound sample starting with signal (s)
> tico2<-cutw(tico, from=0.25)
# running timer() again
> res2 <- timer(tico2,f=22050,threshold=5,msmooth=c(100,0))
# which gives apparently right labels as well
> res2
$s
[1] 0.1408666 0.2135720 0.2999096 0.1772193

$p
[1] 0.20902788 0.16358703 0.24083647 0.09542577

$r
[1] 1.173077

Am I missing somehting?

Thank again for your help,

Best

Jerome
